chunks: And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said:

“The ʿĀqilah is only liable for that which has been established by evidence. And if a man came to him and confessed before him, he assigned it specifically to his own wealth and did not place any of it upon his ʿĀqilah.”

key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: legal evidence or proof establishing a claim
key_terms.الْعَاقِلَةُ: the male kin group who bear blood-money liability in specified cases

ai.seo_question: When is the ʿĀqilah responsible for blood money in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the ʿĀqilah, the male relatives who may bear blood-money liability in certain cases. Their liability is restricted to cases established by proof, whereas a person’s own confession makes the liability rest on his personal wealth, not on his ʿĀqilah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5311 - Commander of the Faithful (as) said:

"The Aqilah (the male relatives responsible for blood money) is only liable for what has been established by evidence. If a man came to him and confessed (to a crime), he made its compensation from his own wealth specifically and did not place any responsibility on his Aqilah for it."
